name: MatterSim (Microsoft Research)
origin_detail: Microsoft Research AI for Science (arXiv:2405.04967, 22 authors led by Han Yang). Built on the M3GNet architecture.
flagship_projects: Advanced versions in Azure Quantum Elements

licences.weights: MIT for the 1M and 5M checkpoints; 'more advanced' versions only in Azure Quantum Elements
licences.data: training data (3M / 6M structures from the MatterSim workflows) not stated as released

openness_notes: Code MIT; the model card lists MIT for the released checkpoints (1M, 5M; both M3GNet-based). The README: 'More advanced and fully-supported pretrained versions of MatterSim, and additional materials capabilities are available in Azure Quantum Elements.' The training data came from the paper's active-learning first-principles workflows (0-5000 K, up to 1000 GPa; PBE); the fetched pages do not say they were released. First public release v1.0.0-rc1, 28 Nov (2024 inferred from a LICENSE.txt commit dated 2024-11-19); preprint 2024-05-08. Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Score 2 (open core).
risk_events: Best versions tied to a commercial cloud product
robustness: Small open checkpoints are forkable; no training data to retrain them.
physical_science_relevance: Atomistic simulation across elements, temperatures and pressures; model card warns of low accuracy for organic polymers.

training_data.name: MatterSim active-learning DFT set (PBE)
training_data.access: not released (not stated on fetched pages)
training_data.note: Training Data Size 3M (1M model) and 6M (5M model); MPtrj and Alexandria are used as test sets.

openness_effect_assessment: Open small checkpoints serve as a funnel to Azure Quantum Elements. Its 612 stars are well below the fully open MatterGen from the same lab (1.9k).
key_takeaway: Within one corporate lab, the model that sits next to a cloud product (MatterSim) is open core, while the one that does not (MatterGen) is fully open.
